mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (proxied by HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between payroll employment (PAYEMS) rising above its 12-month moving average and unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 5% for three consecutive months signals a synchronized labor market tightening, which increases wage growth and input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND UNRATE < 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) below its 5-year average for six consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which dampens consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
